question.text: Arbitragers differ from speculators because arbitragers:

answer.text: Lock in profits by simultaneously entering opposite transactions in two or more markets
Only trade in the spot market

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 95, arbitragers lock in a price difference or profit by simultaneously entering opposite-side transactions in two or more markets and do not carry any underlying exposure. The profit is locked in before costs and execution risk. The Trap: Arbitragers are not the same as hedgers (who have underlying exposure) or speculators (who take directional risk). Note: Pages 95 and 123-124 caution that arbitrage is not strictly risk-free; execution, illiquidity, settlement, transaction-cost and impact-cost risks can all affect realised returns.
